verdict.rationale: npm's docs say it can be pointed at any compatible registry, including a self-run one, and can switch registries even with an existing lock file; a community comment confirms switching is just an `npm config set`. The scoped-authentication half is barely covered: there is only a generic note that `adduser` stores credentials in the user config file, with nothing on per-scope registry mapping or per-registry auth tokens. missing for 10: documented per-scope registry configuration (@scope:registry), per-registry/scoped auth token configuration, explicit mirror/proxy setup guidance, hands-on corroboration of private-registry auth.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can point the manager at private registries or mirrors with scoped authentication

citations.quote: You can configure npm to use any compatible registry you like, and even run your own registry.
If you create a lock file while using the default registry you can switch to another registry and npm will install packages from the new registry
When you do this, npm will store credentials in the user config file.
Switching registries is just an `npm config set`
